In [[mathematics]], a '''measurable acting group''' is a special group that [[Group action (mathematics)|acts]] on some space in a way that is compatible with structures of [[measure theory]]. Measurable acting groups are found in the intersection of measure theory and [[group theory]], two sub-disciplines of mathematics. Measurable acting groups are the basis for the study of invariant measures in abstract settings, most famously the [[Haar measure]], and the study of [[stationary random measure]]s.{{citation needed|date=September 2025}}

== Definition ==
Let <math> (G, \mathcal G, \circ) </math> be a [[measurable group]], where <math> \mathcal G </math> denotes the [[Sigma-algebra|<math> \sigma </math>-algebra]] on <math> G </math> and <math> \circ </math> the [[group law]]. Let further <math> (S, \mathcal S) </math> be a [[measurable space]] and let <math> \mathcal A \otimes \mathcal B </math> be the [[Product sigma-algebra|product <math> \sigma </math>-algebra]] of the <math> \sigma </math>-algebras <math> \mathcal A </math> and <math> \mathcal B </math>.

Let <math> G </math> [[Group action (mathematics)|act]] on <math> S </math> with group action
:<math> \Phi \colon G \times S \to S </math>

If <math> \Phi </math> is a [[measurable function]] from <math> \mathcal G \otimes \mathcal S </math>  to <math> \mathcal S </math>, then it is called a '''measurable group action'''. In this case, the group <math> G </math> is said to act measurably on <math> S </math>.

== Example: Measurable groups as measurable acting groups ==
One special case of measurable acting groups are measurable groups themselves. If <math> S=G </math>, and the group action is the group law, then a measurable group is a group <math> G </math>, acting measurably on <math> G </math>.
